headline: Sunday's front has trended weaker: RRFS dropped its 0.36 in burst to 0.08 in and HRRR now shows almost nothing through Sunday afternoon, so expect a light soaking with no street flooding; channel at base flow.

summary.text: RRFS wettest 3 hours fell from 0.36 to 0.08 in; HRRR, now reaching 4 PM Sunday, shows 0.02 in. No model reaches 0.25 in, so this is no longer a storm watch for the street.
Wettest 3 hours: ECMWF 0.24, GFS 0.14, RRFS 0.08, NBM 0.04, HRRR 0.02 in. ECMWF is the wettest; storm totals 0.03 to 0.52 in.
Rating card consensus about 0.04 in (middle of HRRR 0.02 x 1.25, NBM 0.04, RRFS 0.08): none. Even ECMWF is a third of the 0.71 in Yellow (garage) line.
Dry through Saturday night. Light rain Sunday, heaviest somewhere between about 2 PM and 11 PM depending on the model; showers linger into Monday.
Sunday's 7.9 ft high at 3:33 PM may overlap the ECMWF peak; surge has run 1.2 to 1.4 ft on highs. Channel at Alameda 0.12 ft, far below Monitoring 3.18 ft.
Clearing leaves from street drain grates and yard drains Saturday is still worthwhile. No need to move cars. Avoid the Bay shore at midday high tides through Sunday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: High pressure keeps Saturday dry and mild. A cold front brings rain Sunday, steadier late Sunday afternoon into Sunday night, with gusts of 25 to 35 mph and showers lingering into Monday. NWS San Francisco (long term issued 12:52 PM Friday) expects up to 0.25 in for most of the Bay Area outside the North Bay and the mountains, and calls the rain largely beneficial. The Tuesday system continues to track toward Southern California; NWS now expects only 0.01 to 0.1 in for most of the Bay Area, and it is beyond this 72-hour window.

sections.title: Model trends
sections.text:
From 7 PM Friday to 7 PM Monday, wettest 3 hours / storm total:
• ECMWF: 0.24 / 0.52 in, about 2 to 5 PM Sunday (up from 0.11 / 0.31 in this afternoon).
• GFS: 0.14 / 0.23 in, about 6 to 9 PM Sunday.
• RRFS (10 AM run): 0.08 / 0.14 in, about 3 to 6 PM Sunday (down from 0.36 / 0.57 in).
• NBM: 0.04 / 0.20 in, light and spread out, about 8 to 11 PM Sunday.
• HRRR (5 PM run, ends 4 PM Sunday): 0.02 / 0.03 in.
• HRRR 15-minute (through 11:45 PM Saturday): 0.00 in.

The banded RRFS scenario that prompted this afternoon's discussion has gone away, and HRRR now covers the start of the event with almost no rain. ECMWF moved the other way and is the wettest model, but its biggest hour is 0.08 in, far from the 0.40 in one-hour Yellow trigger. Even allowing for HRRR's history of under-forecasting local bursts, nothing here points to water in the street.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run ends 1 PM Sunday) keeps Redwood City highs 1.2 to 1.4 ft above predictions: Saturday 8.6 ft at 2:27 PM modeled near 9.8 ft, Sunday 7.2 ft at 4:49 AM modeled near 8.6 ft. Sunday's 7.9 ft high at 3:33 PM is beyond the model run. The NWS Coastal Flood Advisory (2:53 PM Friday) for Bayshore locations runs until 5 PM Sunday; it affects the shoreline and tidal sloughs, not Athlone Terrace directly.

Channel at Alameda de las Pulgas: 0.12 ft at 6 PM, flat between 0.10 and 0.13 ft for the past day (Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 PM (Monitoring 2.8 ft), with no rain at its gauge in the past 24 hours.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Nothing urgent for the street. Saturday is a good day to clear leaves from drain grates before the season's next rounds.
• Stay off the Bay shore and low shoreline paths around the midday high tides through Sunday, and drive carefully on wet roads Sunday evening.
• This page will switch back to a storm discussion if the models bring a heavier burst back into the next 72 hours.
